Each dispatch opens a conversation keyed by the job id. The conversation is disposable, carries no history from other jobs, and its prompts are self-contained. A retry of the whole run is a fresh conversation under a suffixed id. The bounds are one hundred turns, authoring one retry, revision two, set in configuration with the model; the model is flash-class, to be chosen by evaluation before the agent round runs. The settled reply is a script validated in-loop by its own tool calls, a not-article verdict from the author, or the agent giving up. The reply never carries units. The workflow runs every settled script through the runtime, so a fresh recipe and a years-old one extract through the same deterministic path.

## 📞 The calling side

The API calls through a thin client: `spawn(html, recipe or none, job id, domain)` at the source step, and `resolve(job id)` on poll. The pipeline maps the states to outcomes and writes the `extraction:`-prefixed errors; the client translates nothing. The item's extraction handle is the job id, stable across retries. A retried item re-attaches to the same running job, and the API mints a new id only when the previous job ended `error`, because that is the one terminal whose instance would hand back the same failure. The item stores the extraction domain beside the handle, because a redirect can leave the item's URL pointing somewhere other than the final host, and the recipe insert at resolve time needs the true domain.

Fetching stays API-side and always uses firecrawl. The queued ceiling measures 300 seconds from `queued_at` and fires during holds too; each accepted retry restarts the clock. A `not_article` verdict fails the item permanently, and the retry route accepts the item under its cap, the verdict included.

> [!NOTE] The ceiling can kill an item mid-authoring
> An authoring that outlasts about four windows exhausts the retry cap, the item dies, and its job completes unread. The recipe the job authored is lost, and the domain's next article authors fresh. Accepted knowingly. Authoring inside one window is the expected case, the turn bound is a ceiling rather than a forecast, and the ceiling's simplicity is worth more than a paused clock.

## ⚙️ Platform limits

A workflow instance has no wall-clock limit; the bound is CPU per invocation, tens of seconds by default and configurable upward. The agent loops never approach that bound, because model turns are input-output waits. Instance parameters, step results and the returned output are each capped near 1 MiB: an article whose fetched HTML exceeds the cap fails as too large before any step runs. Finished outputs persist for the retention window, days on the free tier and a month on the paid tier, which is far longer than the poll's resolve cadence. Instance state is kept for that window too, so a job id is not reusable until the window passes.

## ℹ️ Sources
## ⏳ Deferred work is mortal, and the ceiling recovers it

The task's mortality is the price of running deferred work inside the API process instead of a worker, and two mechanisms pay it.

**The ceiling.** Poll fails an item once its work age passes `NAGARA_QUEUED_CEILING_SECONDS` (default 300), with `enrichment: no result after 300s`, when the item is `queued` or is `generating` while still holding an unresolved extraction job. The ceiling never fails a `generating` item whose extraction handle is cleared and whose synthesis call is in flight. That phase survives an API redeploy, and poll resolves it. An extraction job that outlives the ceiling, such as one whose recipe is still being authored, finishes after the item has already failed, so no poll reads its result; the retry route recovers the item. Work age is `now - queued_at`, never `now - created_at`: `created_at` never moves, so measuring from it would fail a just-retried item instantly and turn retry into a no-op that reports failure. `queued_at` is set in the enqueue write, so even a row stranded before its task ever ran carries a clock the ceiling can read.

**Every task write is conditional on the item still being `queued`.** The writes go through `_write_if_queued`, a single `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'queued'` that checks rowcount. If a slow-but-alive task finishes a minute after poll already tripped the ceiling and marked the item `failed`, its `generating` write matches zero rows and the task abandons, committing nothing further. A late task can never resurrect a failure a client has already observed. A `generating` step runs inside the poll request, which is the item's only writer in that phase, so the step mutates the row directly and the request's own commit persists the change.

> [!WARNING] A late task must not overwrite a failed row
> The subtle case is a container that was slow rather than dead. Without the conditional write, its finishing `UPDATE` would stamp `generating` over the `failed` a poll already surfaced, and a client that surfaced the failure would see the item silently un-fail. The `WHERE status = 'queued'` guard is what forecloses that. SQLite reports changed rows rather than matched rows, which is reliable here because every task write moves at least one column off its previous value.

> [!NOTE] Why nothing sweeps in the background
> The extraction job, the Modal resolution and the ceiling are all computed on poll, when a client asks. An item nobody polls stays where the last write left it, which is acceptable because the state is only needed at the moment it is read. Nothing runs on a timer scanning for work to advance.

> [!TIP] Rejected: a background sweeper polling all in-flight calls
> A sweeper that walked every `queued` and `generating` row would reintroduce a second process the zero-broker approach in [tts-service](tts-service.md) deliberately avoids, for no benefit at this scale. State computed on poll is enough, because poll is exactly when the new state is needed.

## 🔁 Retry resumes from the phase that failed

`POST /items/{id}/retry` re-drives a `failed` item in place. It returns `202` and hands the item to the same task enqueue uses; [item-contract](item-contract.md) carries the route and wire detail.

**Only a `failed` item under the cap is retryable.** `queued`, `generating` and `ready` all return `409`, and so does a `failed` item at or past `retry_max` (default 3). A stranded item needs no special case: the ceiling converts it to `failed` first, which is the whole reason the ceiling exists.

What the retry does depends on how far the row got:

| Row at retry | What happens | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| units and `enriched_at` set | promoted to `generating`; poll spawns synthesis from the units on the row | no fetch, no describe |
| units, no `enriched_at` | promoted to `generating`; poll describes again, then spawns | no fetch |
| no units | back through the fetch and the spawn, re-attaching to the job when a handle survives | one fetch |

The extraction handle is stable across retries, so a retried item re-attaches to the job the first attempt spawned. Only an `error` terminal clears the handle, because that job would hand back the same failure; the retry then mints a new id suffixed with the retry count. A `not_article` verdict keeps its handle, so a retry re-attaches to the job and the item fails again with the same verdict. `queued_at` is rewritten on every attempt, which is why the ceiling measures from it.

> [!WARNING] A retry after a synthesis crash resolves the same crashed call
> A `tts:` failure leaves `modal_call_id` on the row, and the retry does not clear it. The promoted item's next poll resolves that same call, which re-raises the same exception, so the item fails again with the same `tts:` error and never re-spawns synthesis. The retry still returns `202`, and the failure shows only on the following poll.

content.text:
I went through all 36 items from the last week: 26 reached `ready` and 10 failed. Every failure falls into one of three causes, and the first one accounts for 7 of them.

## 1. The 300s ceiling fails items while their recipe is still being written (7 items)

Error: `enrichment: no result after 300s`. Items: the four tej.as items, both quantamagazine/asermax "super intelligence" items, and the first Quanta item.

- **Every one of these extraction jobs succeeded on Cloudflare.** I checked each Workflow instance. Writing a new recipe, or revising an old one, took 2–8 minutes, and every job ended with a working recipe and a title. The API had already marked the item failed on a poll at 300s, so no poll ever read the result.
- **The recipes those jobs wrote were thrown away.** A recipe is only saved when a poll reads the finished job. That's why tej.as and quantamagazine.org still have no recipe: each new article from them will write one from scratch again and hit the same limit.
- **Time spent waiting in the domain queue also counts against the 300s.** You enqueued `itm_f5f0aed0` at the same moment as `itm_0652a301`, but its job only started 6 minutes later, after the other one released the tej.as slot. Re-enqueueing the same URLs made the waits longer.
- **The error text is wrong.** It says `enrichment:`, but these items were waiting on extraction.
- For scale, the successful recipe-writing jobs this week took 40s to 4m48s. bostonreview and ghuntley.com/lisp got through with about 10 seconds to spare.

`docs/technical-design/extraction-service.md` already describes this as "accepted knowingly", on the assumption that writing a recipe usually finishes within one 300s window. This week's runs show it usually doesn't.

## 2. Revision attempts give up with "the reply carried no readable settlement" (2 items)

Items: both asermax.github.io WebMCP items (`itm_3aa6df1b`, `itm_3e19dee7`), which ended in `revision gave up`.

- The first attempt ran for about 3 minutes, then returned text with no settlement in it.
- Attempts 2 and 3 each finished in **2–3 seconds** with the same result. A fresh conversation should not end that fast, so the model call is probably failing quickly, for example with a gateway error or rate limit, and the error text is being treated as the reply.
- I couldn't confirm this: the wrangler login token gets "Authentication error" from the AI Gateway logs API.
- The parser in `pipeline/src/agents/settlement.ts:37` throws the reply text away, so the Workflow step output doesn't show it either.

## 3. Firecrawl failed on The Atlantic gift link (1 item)

Item: `itm_5f75a277`, error `fetch: firecrawl unreachable`. `api/app/service/fetch.py:84` wraps every exception in that one message and logs nothing, and the Railway logs for that minute show only the POST. The real cause is not recorded anywhere.

## Smaller issue

One recipe attempt crashed with `el.clone is not a function`. The prompt tells the agent to "prepare clones" but doesn't say to use `$(el).clone()`. The second attempt fixed it, at the cost of an extra agent turn.

## Proposed fixes

1. **Ceiling:** give items waiting on an extraction job a separate, longer limit, something like `extraction_ceiling_seconds = 1200`, and change their error to `extraction: no result after …`. The 300s limit would still cover the `queued` phase, which exists because background tasks die with the container. The Workflow itself survives redeploys, like synthesis does. This reverses a documented decision, so I'd update `extraction-service.md` and `item-lifecycle.md` in the same change.
2. **Revision "no settlement":**
   - include a short excerpt of the reply in the gave-up reason, so the next failure shows up in the Workflow output;
   - if you add an API token with AI Gateway log read access to `pipeline/.dev.vars`, I can look at the actual replies from Oct 5.
3. **Firecrawl:** log the exception and include its type in the error. I can also run one Firecrawl scrape of the Atlantic URL to reproduce it, which costs a few credits.
4. **Prompt:** say to clone with `$(el).clone()`.

None of the 7 ceiling-failed items can be recovered with a retry. Each retry would reattach to its finished job, but that job's results come from the job index, which keeps them for one day (`indexSweepMs`), and these are older than that.

Should I go ahead with 1–4, and do you want the Firecrawl reproduction and the gateway token?
